We need teach by showing demonstration pairs. We can call show_transformed_input with various inputs. Need infer rule: replace all colored blocks inside rectangular shapes with black so only colored outline of shapes. Verifier: objects(I,T,F,T): univalued True, diagonal False, without_bg True. So connected components of same color non-bg (4-connected). For each object, difference(toindices(obj), box(obj)) = interior cells not on bounding box outline. Fill with mostcolor(I) (background). So it hollows each monochrome rectangular object: keeps its bounding box outline colored (actually keeps original cells that lie on bounding box boundary, sets interior non-boundary cells to bg). Note: if object shape isn't full rectangle? box is bounding box outline; difference removes interior cells not on bbox outline. Cells of object on bbox outline remain. Cells of object inside not on outline become bg. Also if object non-rectangular, cells outside bbox? impossible.

Need produce demo pairs. The student sees only pairs. We should show variety: multiple rectangles, different colors, maybe non-rectangular shapes? Rule says rectangular shapes. Better show rectangular colored shapes on black background. Include cases with multiple shapes, different sizes/colors, shapes not filling entire grid, maybe shapes with holes? The verifier handles univalued 4-connected objects. If two rectangles of different colors touching? They are separate objects. If same color adjacent maybe merge. Need avoid ambiguity.

We want teaching set maybe 5-10 pairs. Let's create inputs and let environment compute output. Must be valid grids rectangular, integers 0-9. Verifier can evaluate. We can call multiple in parallel? The tool calls can be multiple in one block. We need ensure no overlap issues. Let's design several.

Example: 
1) single 3x3 square color 1 on 0. Output outline.
2) two rectangles of different colors separated.
3) a rectangle touching edge? The example rectangle is not touching edge? It touches? rows 1-6, cols 1-6. Not edge? row 0 and 7,8 black. Fine.
4) multiple rectangles same color? If same color and not connected, separate objects.
5) a larger rectangle with interior already black? The input likely solid. But rule "replace all colored blocks inside" works on solid. If already hollow, box outline same. We can show solid.
6) maybe two rectangles adjacent same color touching: would merge into one object; bounding box outline might include gap? Avoid.

We need demonstrate that the shape's outline stays, interior becomes background. Show colors different. Include rectangular shapes of various aspect ratios. Maybe also a shape that is not perfectly rectangular? The rule says rectangular. But verifier objects univalued, box. If input is L-shaped same color, output would keep bbox outline cells that are part of object, and clear interior non-bbox. But cells of L not on bbox outline? If L shape has no interior maybe output same? Not needed.

Maybe include example where rectangle is 2 rows tall: no interior? box difference empty? For height 2, box includes all cells? For 2xN rectangle, box outline includes top and bottom rows, all cells are on box outline, so output same. That could confuse. Better all rectangles at least 3x3.

Also include multiple colors: red, green, blue etc.

Let's think about verifier specifics: objects(I,T,F,T): univalued True, diagonal False, without_bg True. bg=mostcolor(I). If background is most common. If a shape color appears more than background? Unlikely if background large. But if multiple shapes, total colored might exceed background? Could cause mostcolor to be a shape color, then without_bg True would treat that shape color as background and not object? That would break. So ensure background 0 is most common. Keep colored cells less than half.

Also if multiple objects of same color that are separate, they are separate because not connected. Good.

Could also show a single non-rectangular object? The natural language says rectangular shapes. Stick to rectangles.

Number of pairs: maybe 6-8. The student needs infer. Too many may be okay. The scoring includes number of pairs shown. But likely not penalized? "number of pairs you show will also be recorded." Could be good to show enough. We'll show maybe 7.

Potential issue: The verifier's box uses bounding box of object. If a rectangle is not solid? If input has a hollow rectangle already, difference of object indices and box: interior already not colored, so no change. But we show solid.

The environment computes outputs and shows to student. We don't need to wait? We can do all in one block? The tool calls are independent.
